case_name: Gangadhar Behera and others v State of Orissa
respondent:
State of Orissa
Supreme Court of India

10 October 2002
Appeal (Cr.) 1282 of 2001
The Judgment was delivered by: Arijit Pasayat, J.
1. This is the second journey of the accused-appellants to this Court questioning their conviction on being found guilty of offences punishable u/s. 302 read with S. 149 and S. 148 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short "THE IPC").
2. On the first occasion apart from the conviction for the aforesaid offences, the appellants were also convicted u/s. 307 read with S. 149 IPC. However, in the second instance, the said conviction has been altered to one u/s. 324 read with S. 149 IPC.
3. Filtering out unnecessary details, the prosecution version as unfolded during trial is as follows:
4. On 31.12.1988, there was an altercation between Jairam Das and Sadananda (hereinafter referred to as the deceased) on one hand and Jagabandhu Samal (D.W.1) on the other near Motto Hat in connection with occupation/construction of a shed in a mark
holding: The common object of the unlawful assembly can be gathered from the nature of the assembly, arms used by them and the behaviour of the assembly at or before the scene of occurrence.
It is not necessary for the prosecution to prove which of the members of the unlawful assembly did which or what act.
Evidence of eye witnesses is sufficient to fasten guilt by application of S. 149.
